paper.title_en: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe$_2$
paper.abstract_en: The candidate topological superconductor UTe$_2$ exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. In particular, the apparent observation of two intersecting second-order phase boundaries at a triple point in the pressure-temperature phase diagram is thermodynamically forbidden. This suggests either a hidden phase transition or a fundamental misunderstanding of the superconductivity in this material. Here we observe an additional phase boundary that is characterized by an upward jump in the sound velocity. This is direct thermodynamic evidence for a phase transition in which superconducting order is lost on cooling. Our results establish a tetracritical point beyond which the ambient and pressure-induced superconducting order parameters form a multicomponent state. We use the measured phase diagram to demonstrate that strong competition between the two superconducting order parameters drives the loss of order when cooling, and leads to phase locking that suppresses superconducting fluctuations. These findings provide the definitive magnetic field-pressure-temperature phase diagram of UTe$_2$ and establish a thermodynamic foundation for multicomponent superconductivity.
paper.journal_ref: Kamat, S., Dans, J., Saha, S. et al. Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe2. Nat. Phys. (2026)
